title: Code-built menu tree and registry drift
summary: The menu tree a Delphi program builds in code, read statically, and a check that the registered menu paths still match it
intro: Read this when a menu is built in code (TMenuItem.Create, Caption :=, Add) rather than in a .dfm and you need to see the real tree, or when a documented menu path may have drifted from the code. `drag-lint menu-tree --project <dproj> --db <db>` prints the tree: helpers are recognised by what their body does, not by their name, and a caption it cannot evaluate is shown as dynamic with a note instead of being dropped. Needs a fresh project index; a changed file is refused with exit 3.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint menu-tree --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> [--root <QName>] [--format text|json|paths] [--output <f>] (the menu tree a program builds in code, read statically; exit 0 ran, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)
help: drag-lint menu-tree --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> [--root <QName>] [--format text|json|paths] [--output <f>]   (the menu tree a program BUILDS IN CODE, read statically: helpers recognised by body, click wrappers, callbacks, const-array / case captions; a caption it cannot evaluate is a dynamic node + a note; exit 0 ran, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)

surfaces.usage: drag-lint menu-drift --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --registry <features dir> [--format text|json] [--output <f>] (code-built menu tree vs the registry's ide-menu paths: missing / moved / unregistered / notes; exit 0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)
help: drag-lint menu-drift --project <X.dproj> --db <file.sqlite> --registry <features dir> [--format text|json] [--output <f>]   (the code-built menu tree vs the registry's ide-menu PATHS: MISSING (renamed? hint), MOVED (now at), UNREGISTERED (skeleton surface), NOTE; exit 0 no drift, 1 drift, 2 usage/setup, 3 stale index)
